assessment_kind_note: Estimates the LIKELIHOOD of diagnosed cardiac disease. Module 8's RULE_HEART_DISEASE_RISK_FACTORS emits the same condition string from a RISK-FACTOR COUNT. Both are legitimate and they are not the same quantity; the predictor stamps metadata.assessment_kind on every decision so Modules 16/17 can fuse them without conflating burden with probability.

dataset.source: CDC NHANES 2017-2023. Outcome, age, BMI and cholesterol from the Kaggle extract ahiduzzaman28/nhanes-cvd-raw-data-2017-23; sex and smoking joined on SEQN from CDC's own P_DEMO/DEMO_L and P_SMQ/SMQ_L files.
dataset.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 (extract); CDC NHANES is public domain
dataset.outcome_definition: Positive if a doctor ever diagnosed ANY of coronary heart disease, heart attack, angina or congestive heart failure. Negative only if all four were answered 'no'. Stroke is excluded as cerebrovascular.
dataset.age_conversion: none -- NHANES RIDAGEYR/Age is already whole years. v1 had to convert cardio_train's age-in-days.
dataset.cholesterol_semantics: CONTINUOUS total cholesterol in mg/dL. NOT an ordinal band: v1's cardio_train column was 1/2/3 and had to be mapped from mg/dL, which discarded information this dataset preserves.

cleaning_rule.basis: None needed. NHANES publishes examined, quality-controlled measurements; cardio_train required height/weight/BMI bands to remove values incompatible with an adult.

dataset.gender_mapping_basis: DOCUMENTED by CDC in the RIAGENDR codebook -- not inferred. v1's cardio_train mapping had to be inferred from height and smoking rates because that dataset documents nothing.
dataset.smoking_semantics: SMQ020 (smoked 100+ cigarettes ever) with SMQ040 (smokes now: 1 every day, 2 some days, 3 not at all). Current smoker = 1; never and former = 0; refused/don't-know unresolved, selecting the without_smoking variant.

excluded_columns.Systolic_BP / Diastolic_BP: VaidyaAI collects no blood pressure; a model leaning on them could never be fed at inference.
excluded_columns.Vitamin_D / Vitamin_B12: DIETARY INTAKE (mcg/day), not the serum levels VaidyaAI's identically-named features hold. Different quantity.
excluded_columns.C_Reactive: No CRP entry in feature_catalog.py; VaidyaAI cannot supply it.
excluded_columns.nutrition block: Dietary recall; VaidyaAI has no dietary features.
excluded_columns.Stroke: Cerebrovascular, not the cardiac condition Module 8 names.

dataset.resampling: none -- class weights only, no SMOTE, no oversampling

tri_state_policy: An unresolved smoking answer selects the without_smoking variant, which was FITTED without the column. No value is imputed for it, so the model never treats a missing answer as a stated one.
unknown_category_policy: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore'). A gender Module 2 allows but this cohort has no level for (e.g. prefer_not_to_say) becomes an all-zero block rather than the majority category.
cholesterol_semantics: CONTINUOUS total cholesterol in mg/dL -- NOT v1's 1/2/3 NCEP band. Keeping the real number is worth about +0.024 ROC-AUC over banding it. app/ml/heart.py's cholesterol_band() is unused by this artifact.

feature_importance_caveat: Mean impurity decrease over the whole training set. It ranks features FOR THE MODEL and orders the evidence. It is NOT a per-patient explanation.

comparison_to_v1.note: The two numbers are computed on DIFFERENT populations and DIFFERENT outcome definitions, so this is not a like-for-like contest and should not be quoted as one. What can be said: v2 uses the SAME five patient inputs as v1 -- nothing was given up -- learns them from a nationally representative cohort with a stated diagnostic outcome, and does so at a realistic 9% prevalence rather than a constructed 50%.

blood_pressure_reference_model.measured_on: this cohort, same test rows for both models
blood_pressure_reference_model.why_not_shipped: VaidyaAI collects no blood pressure anywhere -- not in Module 2's profile and not from a lab report -- so every patient would arrive with it missing and the pipeline would median-impute it for all of them.
blood_pressure_reference_model.supersedes_v1_estimate: v1 recorded the cost of this exclusion as about 0.10 ROC-AUC, and the project has since treated adding a systolic field to Module 2 as the highest-value change available to Module 11. On THIS cohort the measured cost is far smaller -- see roc_auc_cost_of_exclusion. The 0.10 figure is a property of cardio_train, where blood pressure carried most of the signal and the remaining features carried little; it does not transfer. Blood pressure is still worth having, but on this evidence it is a small gain, and the case for changing the profile should be argued from this number rather than from the inherited one.

honest_read: Held-out ROC-AUC above 0.82 at a realistic 9% prevalence. That is a usable coarse discriminator and nothing more: PR-AUC around 0.32 against a 0.09 baseline means most people it ranks highly will still not have heart disease, so a high score is a reason to discuss testing with a clinician, never a finding. It learned from what respondents said a doctor had told them, so it under-counts exactly the people a screening tool most wants to find.
